summary: RAG + dimensional guided schema, 7 typed slots
hypothesis: Forcing seven named per-dimension schema slots (goal/scope/who-for/budget/timeline/current-state/constraints) should structurally guarantee coverage breadth, because the 3B model lacks the judgment to rank which unknown is critical and freely drops important dimensions when given a flat array.
technique: Built on the exp011 RAG+contrastive base, replaced the flat `questions: [FMQuestion].count(7)` array with seven distinctly `@Guide`-typed slots — one per universal high-value planning dimension — so the schema structurally enforces each dimension's presence at compile time, not via prompting or runtime instruction.
result: Scored 0.243 on dev-10 (0 wins / 0 ties / 10 losses vs Sonnet), the worst non-pipeline variant and −0.077 below the exp003/exp011 plateau of ~0.32. Coverage stayed at 3 while specificity and naturalness also lagged; the fixed universal slots injected irrelevant questions (budget into bakery-naming, who-for into weddings) and crowded out task-critical unknowns. Hypothesis falsified — discarded.
